Hi, I'm Maya. I travel to work on the 38 bus every day. There's a transfer at Van Ness — the platform has no shelter — and the full journey takes about fifty minutes each way.
The Van Ness transfer is the unreliable part. If the connecting bus is delayed I can lose another fifteen or twenty minutes standing on that exposed platform.
My IT band has flared up again. I've had this problem before — it's a sharp pain on the outside of my knee that gets worse when I try to run or climb stairs quickly.
I've got a physio appointment booked for next Thursday. In the meantime I've had to stop running completely — I was doing three runs a week before this flared up.
I got a letter from my landlord yesterday — rent is going up by eighty pounds a month from the first of next month. I wasn't expecting it to be that much.
I've been in this flat for three years and this is the second increase. I need to find savings somewhere or look at whether I can negotiate with the landlord.
I started a spending diary this week to track every purchase. Looking at the food column — pastries at the station, sandwiches at lunch, drinks on the way back — it's thirty to forty pounds a week.
That's money I wouldn't spend if I cooked at home. I've thought about batch cooking on Sundays but I haven't actually done it yet.
It rained heavily on Tuesday and I got completely soaked — my jacket was wet through and I had to change when I arrived. The umbrella barely helped because the wind was strong.
The forecast says more rain on Thursday and Friday. It's been overcast all week and I find it harder to feel alert when there's no sunlight at all.
I've been on closing shifts three nights this week — finishing at ten, sometimes quarter past. By the time I get back to the flat I have zero interest in standing at the cooker.
I stop at the corner shop on the way home — chips, a ready meal, whatever needs no preparation. It's happening two or three nights a week and the cost is adding up.
The connecting bus at Van Ness has been delayed repeatedly this week — twice it was over fifteen minutes late. On opening shift days I absolutely cannot miss that connection.
I've started leaving the flat ten minutes earlier on opening shift days to build in a buffer. That puts me out the door before five o'clock, which means there's no time to do anything before I leave.
